page: Microsoft Azure D128ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes a massive 480 MB L3 cache. Storage is bundled with 7559 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, though it does not include any dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scores all ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, achieving top-tier results for both small-block cached and large-block uncached read and write operations. While single-core performance in stress-ng and text generation for large language models falls into the average category, the server excels in database operations, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations, all of which place in the top 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D128ds_v7 offers high resource density by combining a massive 128-vCPU compute allocation with a substantial local NVMe SSD storage tier. This configuration avoids the premium cost of dedicated GPU hardware while delivering top-tier throughput for data-intensive tasks. It is highly suited for large-scale database hosting, high-throughput static web serving, multi-threaded data compression, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
